head: cloud/http-header-name-token
title: fix(serve): reject HTTP header names that are not tokens
body:
The request parser in `HttpServer::handle_connection` accepted any non-empty text before the first `:` as a header name. A request with `Transfer-Encoding : chunked` or `Content-Length\t: 5` therefore stored a name with trailing whitespace, which no header lookup matched. The request went through as if it had no body (200), where RFC 9112 §5.1 requires a 400. The same applied to a name containing a space, and to an obsolete folded continuation line that contains a colon.

Every response already sends `Connection: close`, so this is a protocol-conformance fix, not a request-smuggling fix: such requests now get the existing 400 for malformed headers.

Change: a header name must be a non-empty RFC 9110 token (alphanumerics plus ``!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~``). Otherwise the existing `valid_headers = false` path rejects the request.

Test: `TestFramingAndMetrics` adds four cases to its malformed-header list: `Transfer-Encoding : chunked`, `Content-Length\t: 5`, a folded continuation line, and `Bad Name: x`. On unpatched main the test aborts at the first new case (status 200 instead of 400).

Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.
